summary: Kickoff for a 4-week POC focused on security gating and performance benchmarks. Agreed acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, correctness), an initial benchmark window, and deliverables: security docs, sample workloads, and a benchmark plan. Key security topics: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML with IdP, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM requirements, and data residency concerns for EU traffic.
topics: deployment mode options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evan Chen (Aperture CTO), Mira Patel (Aperture Head of Security), Lukas Novak (Aperture ML Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood side, and Priya will run the bench/security tech parts. Evan, Mira — thanks for taking time. can you do a quick round?
[00:14] Evan: yeah sure, I'm Evan, CTO at Aperture. we're a B2B visual search startup, lots of PII in metadata, predominantly eu users. mira — do you want to intro from security?
[00:23] Mira: hi all, Mira Patel, head of security. primary concerns: SOC 2 coverage, ISO 27001 alignment, strong SSO/SAML integration, RBAC for dev vs product vs analytics, audit log retention for 12 months, and KMS integration for keys. also data residency for eu traffic.
[00:40] Priya: great, thanks. quick note on workload: Lukas, can you describe typical request sizes, average tokens, qps, any heavy context windows?
[00:50] Lukas: sure. most requests are short: avg 60 tokens in prompt, 40 tokens response. we do some long prompt sessions like 1024 tokens for batch inference for re-ranking, but those are <5% of traffic. baseline traffic is bursty, typical sustained 25 qps, peak 120 qps for 30-90s. latency is important, target p95 under 300ms for the short path.
[01:12] Jordan: helpful. our goal today is to align on security gating for the pilot and nail down benchmark success criteria and a timeline for the 4-week pilot. i'll start with security posture and what we can provide.
[01:23] Jordan: Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate summary, an SSO/SAML integration guide, and our RBAC model in the console. We also have audit logs accessible via our console and can stream to your SIEM (syslog/S3). note: for KMS, we support customer-managed keys in our Private deployments and KMS integrations in Dedicated.
[01:41] Mira: couple clarifying q's — 1) for the Hosted API, are keys ever stored in plaintext in our region? 2) can you provide audit log retention configuration and export endpoints?
[01:50] Priya: good q. Hosted keys are encrypted at rest; we do allow bring-your-own-key on Dedicated/Private. audit logs can be configured to 12 months in our enterprise plan and we can ship them to S3 or a SIEM via secure transfer. i will put exact endpoints and retention options in the doc.
[02:09] Mira: do you support SAML with our IdP (okta) and SCIM for user provisioning?
[02:14] Jordan: yes — SAML SSO with Okta is supported, SCIM provisioning is available for role mapping. small caveat: in hosted we enforce our RBAC layers; Dedicated/Private lets you control more granular network policies.
[02:26] Lukas: technical note — for the benchmark we need to test both short-gen path and re-ranking. For re-ranking we use KV cache heavily — does Redwood maintain warm KV cache across requests in dedicated?
[02:36] Priya: yes, we maintain KV cache across warm workers; for Dedicated we can reserve capacity to reduce cold starts. sometimes auto-scaling can evict, but we'll configure bump-up for the POC run.
[02:47] Evan: ok on the benchmarks — let's talk numbers. our acceptance criteria: sustained 30 qps for short path with p95 < 300ms and p99 < 600ms, and re-rank batch of 16 documents p95 < 700ms. cost target is also important but secondary.
[03:06] Jordan: sounds reasonable. we'll propose a benchmark plan that includes a warm-up phase, two steady-state runs, and a stress run. we also want to validate correctness/regression: your golden prompts + expected outputs for a sample set.
[03:19] Mira: on compliance, we need to confirm: 1) where data at rest is stored for eu traffic, 2) encryption algorithm details, 3) if Redwood's staff can access logs/keys, and 4) proof of regular pen tests.
[03:31] Priya: answers: data residency — Hosted has regional controls; we can pin to eu-west region. encryption — AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit. staff access — role-based access is audited; we have a vault and SSO backed sessions, privileged access is rare and logged. pen tests — yes, annual third-party pen testing; i'll include the summary and contact.
[03:50] Evan: good. timeline? you mentioned a 4-week POC. break that out for us.
[03:55] Jordan: Week 0 (this week): security docs exchange and onboarding, set up test accounts + SSO. Week 1: baseline benchmark (short path & re-rank), Week 2: tuning (batching, quantization advice), Week 3: verification runs + regression checks, Week 4: final report and decision meeting. we can compress if both teams agree.
[04:18] Lukas: for tuning, can you recommend quantization levels? we prefer int8 if possible. also want to try continuous batching and measure impact on latency.
[04:26] Priya: we'll recommend quantization and model variant for the workload; Dedicated supports int8 quantization, and we can test both fp16 and int8. continuous batching config will be part of the benchmark scripts.
[04:36] Mira: RBAC question — we need to segregate access: dev env people can query models but can't access audit logs; security team can see logs but not query production models. is that supported?
[04:46] Jordan: yes, console RBAC supports role scopes — we'll share the mapping. also our audit logs can be set to redact certain fields if needed.
[04:54] Evan: what about private deployment option? for data residency and keys, we might want Private (VPC) — what's the deployment effort?
[05:02] Priya: Private deployment requires a short checklist — network peering, firewall rules, KMS configuration. typical turn-up is 2-4 weeks in parallel with the POC if you want full isolation. Dedicated is faster to stand up and gives many controls with less lead time.
[05:17] Mira: if we do Private, we need an on-prem option for air-gapped infra later — is there a path?
[05:21] Jordan: yes, we have an on-prem package for regulated customers, but that typically moves to a separate contract and ~8-12 week timeline. for this POC, Private VPC is common tradeoff.
[05:30] Evan: can we do a single 2-hour benchmark window with Redwood running the scripts and Aperture running telemetry capture?
[05:35] Priya: yes, propose two 1-hour runs separated by a 30-min pause: first run baseline fp16, second run int8 + batching. we'll collect p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu utilization, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1k tokens.
[05:48] Lukas: also track cold start tail latency over the run. we want to see how KV cache warming affects p99.
[05:53] Priya: noted. we'll instrument KV cache hit rates in the logs. sometimes transcriber may say K-V cash but it's K-V cache, sorry.
[06:00] Mira: one more compliance item — audit log retention must be tamper-evident and we need chain-of-custody for logs for 12 months. can you provide immutability guarantees?
[06:09] Priya: we can write logs to append-only S3 with object lock for retention windows; that'll meet tamper-evidence. we'll detail the implementation in the security pack.
[06:18] Jordan: ok, next: acceptance criteria recap so it's explicit in CRM: 1) Functionality: SSO/SAML working and RBAC configured; 2) Security: SOC2 docs provided, audit log export to S3 + retention 12mo; 3) Performance: short path sustaining 30 qps with p95 < 300ms and p99 < 600ms; re-rank batch16 p95 < 700ms; 4) Correctness: <2% regression on scoring for golden set.
[06:44] Evan: sounds good. on correctness, we'll provide the golden set and thresholds. on pricing — we'll expect a pilot rate during POC, can you send pricing guidance?
[06:52] Jordan: yes we'll send a pilot pricing sheet. also include burst/bucket model for Dedicated.
[06:58] Mira: are there SLA windows for Dedicated? we need 99.9% uptime for production if we scale after pilot.
[07:04] Priya: Dedicated has SLA options; we'll include the SLA appendix in the pack.
[07:08] Evan: ok let's lock timeline: security docs by Friday (2027-06-11), sample workloads by Monday (2027-06-14), bench window week of 2027-06-21. we reconvene 1 week after bench for results.
[07:21] Jordan: perfect. i'll send calendar invites after the call. any final q's?
[07:24] Mira: none from me.
[07:26] Lukas: all set. thanks.
[07:28] Jordan: thanks everyone — end.

Action items repeated verbally and will be in calendar notes. Transcript notes: occasional filler words, speaker overlaps, and minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., K-V cash vs KV cache).
